title: Blended capacity pricing and metering tagging for hosted + dedicated failover
creator: Priya Shah
description: When runtime routes or falls back requests between Hosted API and Dedicated pools (for capacity, region failover, or cost-driven routing), the metering pipeline must reliably tag usage with the effective capacity source and apply the correct unit price. This ticket designs and implements a canonical labeling and post-processing reconciliation flow so invoices and per-token chargebacks reflect blended usage accurately and deterministically even across streaming sessions, mid-stream handoffs, and transient retries.
scope: Design header and ledger tag (capacity_source, pool_id, effective_rate_key), update ingress to emit tags, extend aggregator to preserve source affinity across retries and reconnects, implement post-billing recalculation for confirmed mid-session handoffs, and add audit/alert rules for mismatches between routed capacity and billed capacity.
out_of_scope: Changing pricing models or customer contractual rate negotiation flows; complex invoicing UI changes (billing backend only).
acceptance_criteria: Ingress adds deterministic capacity_source and pool_id tags for every request path (hosted|dedicated|dedicated-fallback)
Metering ledger entries include effective_rate_key and can be joined with routing traces to prove origin at token granularity for both HTTP and streaming sessions

When a mid-session handoff occurs, the pipeline creates a single canonical session id and prorates tokens between sources; ledger shows pre- and post-handoff subtotals and a final blended total that matches expected invoice math
Retroactive adjustments (up to 24h window) can be emitted when replayed routing decisions change cost attribution; adjustments are idempotent and annotated with audit_reason
End-to-end test harness validates semantics for HTTP, WS streaming, and proxy-reencoded sessions including reconnect, retry, and speculative replays
No customer sees double-charges from transient retries or when routing mismatch occurs (fuzz tests below show 0% double-charge cases in 10k simulated sessions)
technical_design_notes: We will add a small immutable routing header (X-RW-CAP-SOURCE) at the edge when the request is assigned a capacity plane. For dedicated pools an additional X-RW-POOL-ID will be attached. The metering producer will persist these tags into the token ledger rows. For streaming handoffs the edge will emit a HANDOFF marker with previous_pool_id and new_pool_id; the ledger ingestor will record token ranges with source attribution. Post-billing reconciliation job computes blended_price = sum(tokens_source_i * price_source_i) / total_tokens and emits adjustment rows if routing traces disagree with initial tags. Edge-case: ephemeral proxy rewrites and rerouting during reconnects require that we carry a preserved session_uuid in the reconnect path; sequence-window anchoring will be used to avoid overlapping token attribution. Privacy constraint: no customer PII should be included in tags.
implementation_steps: Add X-RW-CAP-SOURCE and X-RW-POOL-ID propagation at edge router (API gateway layer)
Extend request envelope schema in metering-producer to include capacity tags (string fields)
Update ledger schema indexes to support queries by pool_id and rate_key (no customer-visible schema migration)
Implement HANDOFF marker handling in streaming ingestor that splits token ranges deterministically
Add post-billing reconciliation job (reconciliation-worker) that consumes routing traces and ledger rows and emits adjustment entries
Create e2e test harness that simulates hosted->dedicated and dedicated->hosted handoffs across HTTP and WS, including retries and reconnects
Instrument dashboards and alerts for reconciliation delta > 0.1% across last 24h by tenant and pool
test_plan: Unit tests for header propagation, integration tests for ingestor split logic, property-based tests simulating reconnects and midstream handoffs, and production shadow run for 48h on 10% of traffic comparing current billing vs blended-billing output before flipping adjustments on. Metrics collected: mismatch_rate, adjustment_volume, and double_charge_rate.
monitoring_and_rollout: Start with shadow mode and reconciliation-only alerts; after 48h and delta <0.05% promote to binary adjustments for non-enterprise tenants; enterprise customers will continue to receive reconciliation reports for 30 days before auto-adjustments are enabled. Rollback playbook includes disabling reconciliation worker and reverting routing header propagation at edge.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Over- or under-billing transient customers during rollout. Mitigation: start with read-only reconciliations and keep a 24h manual review window for adjustments > $500

Risk: Missing session_uuid across proxies leads to orphaned token ranges. Mitigation: enforce session_uuid preservation in gateway and fall back to trace-anchored best-effort reconstructions labeled as 'best-effort' in ledger
Risk: Performance impact on metering pipeline due to added tags. Mitigation: keep tags compact, add indexes incrementally, and benchmark at scale before full rollout
